newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt wants to cut baseline spending -Delamere.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt wants to cut baseline spending -Delamere.

text.p: Assistant Treasurer Tuariki John Delamere said on Monday the New Zealand government is committed to cutting baseline spending.
In a speech to a business forum, he said there was no automatic right to spend the taxpayers' hard earned dollar.
"All government expenditure must be justified and is open to contest every year by Treasury ministers as far as I am concerned.
"I have said before and I say again tonight, that my way of thinking is that every dollar spent should be generating at least $1.20 worth of benefit, otherwise we should not be spending it," he said.
But he added there should be no doubt that the government planned to spend more "because there are some areas of critical need out there and we were elected to find solutions to them."
